patch_description: The current program spends 20s in a best-of-K random perturbation loop that converges to mediocre local optima (~0.03 normalized). Two targeted improvements: (1) cut the time budget to 10s (eval_time is secondary but the 20s budget mainly buys redundant restarts, and 0.71 < the 0.76 of the faster program, so time isn't buying quality); (2) append a deterministic geometric polish stage that directly attacks the argmin (worst) triplet: move each of its three points along the unit perpendicular direction away from the opposite side — the exact direction gradient of the triangle's area — with a shrinking step size. This "worst-triangle expansion" polish is the classical refinement for Heilbronn-style max-min problems and squeezes out extra area after the stochastic search stalls, since increasing the smallest triangle's area only ever requires moving its own three points.
